key_insight: At initial physician evaluation, Dr. CaBot and pediatric emergency physicians each generated high-scoring differential diagnoses in 95% of cases.
clinical_relevance: Agentic AI may support pediatric emergency diagnostic reasoning, but improved patient care has not been demonstrated.
method: Retrospective study of 100 age-stratified, randomly selected pediatric emergency patients subsequently admitted to surgery or inpatient care.
Compared Dr. CaBot, with and without literature search, against four attending pediatric emergency physicians across four documentation touchpoints.
Two independent physician reviewers scored ranked differentials of up to five diagnoses, masked to their source.
evidence_signal: At the primary touchpoint, the difference in high-scoring differentials was 0 percentage points (95% CI: −5.8 to 5.8); reviewer agreement had a weighted kappa of 0.64.
watch_item: This single-center, retrospective evaluation of admitted patients requires prospective validation before conclusions about real-world safety or patient benefit.
paper_title: Agentic AI versus pediatric emergency physicians for differential diagnosis of acutely ill and injured children
